THIS IS THE LAST HOURLY OF THE SESSION and the handoff matters more than usual: the 15:33 pre-close is twelve minutes out and owns three things this run deliberately did not do - the overnight hold decision on OKLO written as a decision rather than a default, the moves.json straddle-and-spot pass on SMCI, and the pruning of the SMCI row once tonight's print has passed. The two-per-complex cap is untouched either way - it guards stops gapping together in a DECLINE, which 8/10 demonstrated across three unrelated stories, and neither an up-move dispersing nor an up-move re-converging is the case it was written for. THE RANK INVERTED BACK. SMR at +6.54% has retaken the lead from OKLO at +6.09%, one hour after OKLO passed it for the first time today. It is 8.42 now, so it was not even unchanged, and the caution was worth writing for the right reason. NO ENTRY, AND THE BAR WAS NOT CLOSE. The mid-session bar is higher than the open's by design; the daily entry mandate discharges through the open slot, which closed at the staleness guard 247 minutes late today and is not reopenable by this run; the nuclear cap would permit exactly one of SMR or LEU beside this position; AMD at 474.51 is 46.8% of the account against a 40% single-name ceiling; and options remain refused on spread and were deliberately NOT re-quoted, because nothing is proposed and a quote pulled only to decorate a refusal is not evidence. It does mean this board should stop describing co-movement as though it were uniform, because on this tape it is not, and where a quoted number and a written thesis disagree the number decides. account.operatorNote: OPERATOR, 2026-08-10, answering the funding escalation carried in the notes above rather than editing either of them. The 900.00 is a deposit I made; the account is funded to about 1000 and the cash is spendable. This answers the deposit and NOTHING ELSE - it is not an authorisation for the OKLO order the 10:46 sync found, which no run here published and which arrived through the same agentic channel escalated on 8/7; that escalation stands open and unanswered. Three rule changes go with it and all three are written up in docs/RULES.md with their arithmetic, because a licence recorded without its constraints is how this record stops being worth reading. The position ceiling goes from two to four, capped at 40% in any one name and at two names in any one complex - the complex cap is the one that matters on a board whose whole universe moves together. Overnight holds are not a change: they were always allowed, the five-session time stop stands, and it is not extendable by conviction. The objective is still about 10% a day, which is roughly 101 dollars at this size and needs a fully deployed four-name book to average +10% in a session against a +20% take-profit; where the objective and the rulebook conflict, the rulebook wins and the retro records the shortfall. What the deposit does NOT do is reopen options - that refusal has been on spread for three sessions, most recently 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling, and no balance narrows a spread. The 10:22 hourly was right to escalate this rather than size against it.

entryWatch.setup: The open slot did not fire in its window - the entry mandate is unmet for 2026-08-11
entryWatch.trigger: None, and deliberately none. The staleness guard closed that slot at 13:40 ET, 247 minutes after 09:33. It is not reopenable later in the day by this run or any other: the mid-session slots are exits-only and the pre-close may not open a position in the last thirty minutes.
entryWatch.why: CARRIED FORWARD UNCHANGED BY THE LAST SLOT OF THE DAY THAT COULD PLAUSIBLY HAVE ARGUED FOR IT, WHICH IS WHY IT STAYS ON THE BOARD. The mandate says standing aside is not available to the open slot; the guard says a run far outside its window publishes nothing; the guard won by its own terms this morning and the day therefore has no specification. This 15:21 hourly is explicitly NOT a second chance at it, and neither is the 15:33 pre-close, which may not open a position in the last thirty minutes. So 2026-08-11 closes with the mandate undischarged and the reason on the record rather than inferred. An entry written here would be a mid-session entry wearing the open's label - the same corruption of the record the guard refused at 13:40, reached by a different route. THE CAUSE IS UPSTREAM OF JUDGEMENT AND IS THE KNOWN ONE: the scheduler is a desktop task that fires only while the operator's app is open, and five slots today - the open and four hourlies - produced no row at all before 13:40. The 14:17 and 15:17 hourlies have since both fired inside their windows, four minutes late each. Three consecutive on-time runs after five silent slots is a better afternoon, not a fix, and the escalation stands.

That pass belongs to the 15:33 pre-close, twelve minutes out, which is also the run that prunes this row once the print has passed.
